title: Consequential destructive confirmation
summary: Confirm destructive actions when the consequence is difficult to reverse, using explicit object and action wording and a safe focus model.
problem: Generic confirmation dialogs fail to communicate scope and can make destructive actions visually equivalent to cancel.
use_when: Deletion or change is irreversible or expensive to recover
The action affects multiple objects, access, billing, or important user data
avoid_when: The action is easily reversible with a reliable undo
Repeated confirmations would create habituation for low-risk actions
rationale: Confirmation should exist for consequence, not merely because an action is red.
Specific wording helps users verify scope before commitment.

use_if: Deletion or change is irreversible or expensive to recover
The action affects multiple objects, access, billing, or important user data
prefer_alternatives_if: A reliable immediate undo can make the action safer with less interruption

requirements: A modal confirmation must manage focus and keep background content inert.
Provide a visible close or cancel path.
Return focus meaningfully when the dialog closes.
keyboard: Escape closes or cancels when safe and consistent with dialog behavior.

requirements: Name the affected object and consequence.
Keep cancel visually and structurally clear.
Do not preselect the destructive action when accidental confirmation risk is high.
